messages:
clara: Heads up — during tonight's EU maintenance we saw a weird spike in GPU pod evictions when drains hit; ~18% more evictions vs normal and a pile of late-binding batches failed to get scheduled before pods were deleted. noticing most failures are in eu-west1-c AZ group.
ben: ugh. did drain run concurrently across AZs or was it staggered?
clara: concurrent. ops-schedule kicked off parallel drains for nodes with "gpu-k80" taint. autoscaler also did a shrink step at the same time.
jia: exact failure mode? pods got Evicted with reason "NodeUnderMaintenance" or status started Terminating before scheduler could place them?
clara: logs show Terminating -> Evicted. scheduler tried to rebind but there wasn't enough contiguous GPU capacity in that AZ; many jobs are late-bound (no nodeSelector) and their scoring prefers same-az because of local NFS for checkpoints.
ben: so two issues: 1) simultaneous drains across AZs reduced cross-AZ spare capacity; 2) affinity/latency preference to same-az prevented easy rebinding.
jia: can we mitigate quickly by: a) pause drains in one AZ, b) bump scheduler soft-affinity weights to allow cross-az placement for late-binding batch jobs, c) add a short drain-backoff annotation so drains retry after Xs if eviction rate > threshold?
clara: we paused remaining drains after noticing the spike. ops-bot: scheduled-drain-job/31122233 started, status: running, targets: eu-west1-{a,b,c}.
ben: for a short-term patch I can flip the scoring for batch priority class to reduce same-az bias. also we should adjust node drain concurrency in the maintenance controller from 5 -> 1 per AZ.
jia: long-term we should: 1) expose per-az drain concurrency and a backoff if eviction-rate > 5%/min, 2) add a label-based exception for late-binding ops to tolerate cross-az placement, 3) surface a "gpu-frag-risk" alert in console when compact GPUs < X% free.
clara: agreed. also we hit a kubelet bug where `--eviction-hard` lines were too aggressive for ephemeral disk and triggered earlier than expected; not directly GPU but accelerated churn. opened GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-ops/issues/468
ben: quick command we used to pause drains: `kubectl annotate nodepool eu-west1-a maintenance/pause=true --overwrite`
jia: I'll draft a small controller change: if pending evictions in last 5m > threshold then mark drain as backoff and reschedule for +10m. psuedo: ```
if (evictionRate > 0.05) {
  drain.backoff = now + 10m
  emit("drain.backoff", nodepool)
}
```
clara: nice. also we should add an autoscaler pre-check: if scheduled drains + shrink would reduce GPU slots below reserved capacity for Dedicated customers -> abort shrink.
ben: scheduling tweak: change soft-affinity weight from 100 -> 30 for jobs with label `workload/late-bind=true` so they can spread across AZs in emergencies. I'll open PR.
ops-bot: autoscaler: shrink aborted for eu-west1 (would breach reserved_capacity=120 GPUs).
jia: can someone run a small canary tomorrow: run parallel drains with concurrency=1 and apply the soft-affinity change to a subset of batch jobs and watch evictions for 1h.
clara: schedule the canary at 0300 UTC. ben, can you own rollout?
ben: on it. will open the PR, add rollout plan, and post a short runbook for oncall to roll back affinity if it causes perf regressions.
clara: thanks — big takeaway: avoid cross-AZ concurrent drains when GPUs are near capacity and prefer backoff logic over aggressive parallel drains.
ops-bot: incident-note created: incident/2026-03-20-eu-drain-evict-spike, severity: S2, assignees: clara, ben, jia.
